textbook:
Clean cutaway textbook illustration of a SINGLE Giardia lamblia trophozoite (the binucleate flagellated gut parasite), shown from a straight-on VENTRAL angle so the bilateral mirror symmetry is immediately obvious, centered and large in a square 1:1 1080x1080 frame with generous negative space around it for later labels. House style: semi-flat vector-style shading with THIN, CRISP, FINE dark outlines - delicate line weight, NEVER thick heavy black cartoon strokes - every structure carrying its own distinct, clearly readable soft colour fill with gentle soft shading. Refined, elegant and scientific. Muted, sophisticated, slightly desaturated educational palette (soft dusty tints, never bright primary or cartoon colours) on a neutral dark charcoal uncluttered background that fills the frame edge-to-edge - no border, no frame, no vignette, no sheet lying on a surface.

IMPORTANT - THIS IS A SCIENTIFIC DIAGRAM, NOT A CARTOON CHARACTER: the two nuclei are internal organelles that merely happen to look like a pair of eyes. Do NOT give the cell a face. No mouth, no smile, no eyebrows, no pupils looking at the viewer, no cheeks, no facial expression, no limbs. The adhesive disc must never read as a mouth.

BODY SHAPE - get this exactly right: the cell is BILATERALLY SYMMETRIC about a vertical midline, a clean TEARDROP / PEAR outline, broad and smoothly rounded at the front (anterior) end and tapering to a narrow point at the back (posterior) end. Dorsal surface smoothly convex; ventral surface flat to gently concave. Warm translucent ivory-tan cytoplasm.

REQUIRED STRUCTURES, all clearly separated and labellable:
1. TWO NUCLEI as a mirror-image pair side by side near the broad anterior end, symmetric either side of the midline - soft violet-blue ovals, each with a small deeper indigo dot (the karyosome) at its centre. Exactly two, equal in size, level with each other.
2. The VENTRAL ADHESIVE DISC on the flat underside: one large CIRCULAR, gently concave, muted teal-grey suction pad occupying most of the anterior-to-mid ventral surface, filled with fine even spiralling microtubule ridges. It is a solid, uniformly-lit, shallow saucer - there is no hole, no aperture, no dark centre, no slit. Its centre is the SAME colour as the rest of the disc.
3. The MEDIAN BODY: a curved, claw-shaped bundle of microtubules, dusty rose, lying ON the midline in the rear half of the cell, drawn STRICTLY INSIDE the cell outline - it must never poke out through the body wall or read as an external appendage.
4. FLAGELLA - THE MOST IMPORTANT CHECKABLE DETAIL: the cell has EXACTLY EIGHT flagella, arranged as FOUR mirror-image PAIRS (2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8). In the finished picture there must be exactly EIGHT free whip-like tips - count them, no more than eight. Pale amber-cream, long, smooth, individually distinct and well separated. The four pairs: an ANTERIOR pair emerging near the front, one on each side, sweeping back alongside the body; a POSTEROLATERAL pair emerging from the mid-body, one on each side, angled outward and back; a VENTRAL pair emerging beneath the mid-body, one each side, trailing along the underside; and a CAUDAL pair emerging together from the tapered posterior tip and trailing straight out behind. Never draw a dense fringe, a bundle of many fine strands, a mane, or radiating rays.


FLAGELLA COUNT - FINAL AND MOST IMPORTANT CHECK: ALL FOUR PAIRS MUST EMERGE FROM THE BODY AND TRAIL FREELY OUTSIDE THE CELL OUTLINE. Do NOT leave the ventral pair hidden as internal lines inside the cytoplasm - it must exit from beneath the lower rim of the adhesive disc, one on each side, and trail visibly outside the silhouette. When the picture is finished, exactly EIGHT separate free flagellar tips must be countable in open space outside the cell body: TWO upper tips (anterior pair), TWO mid-side tips (posterolateral pair), TWO lower-side tips emerging from below the disc (ventral pair), and TWO tips from the posterior point (caudal pair). 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8 visible free ends. Not six, not ten - exactly eight. Keep them long, smooth, well separated and clearly distinguishable from one another.
Do NOT draw: a single nucleus; asymmetric or unequal nuclei; an amoeba shape with pseudopods; a coat of short cilia all over the surface; a bacterial cell wall or nucleoid; a virus capsid; mitochondria with cristae; MORE THAN EIGHT flagella; the disc on the dorsal instead of the ventral surface. Anatomically faithful, single specimen only, no duplicates. Absolutely NO text, letters, numbers, labels, scale bars, arrows or watermarks in the image.
